note: Verified packaged products from Open Food Facts, for the Asian countries other than Malaysia — the companion crawl to packaged-off-my.json. Every row is a published panel off a real pack: the barcode is in source, and nothing here is estimated. Two arithmetic gates threw rows out, and they catch different faults. 4·carbs + 4·protein + 9·fat has to land within 25% of the stated energy; and carbs + protein + fat has to fit inside the serving they sit in, which is what catches a panel inflated in step with its own energy — self-consistent, and still impossible. A third gate is magnitude: an OFF record can pass both and still be a per-serving figure typed into the per-100 g column, which is how malt powder reads 189 kcal/100 g and butter 185, so each row is checked against a plausible range for the kind of food it is. Records with no serving are kept only where the pack is plainly one serving — a 60 g snack bag, a 250 ml carton; a multi-serve pack with no declared portion was skipped rather than given an invented one. The country is in aliases so the row is findable by origin, along with the product's own-language name where the record carried one.
